A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same USCNet research, dataset and CSCS metric. All 24 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component and backbone ablations, generalization experiments, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and additionally reports cross-task misdetection experiments using original pretrained and USC12K-trained models.

M1.justification: The encoder, adapters, frozen decoder and query-attention pipeline are retained; APG/SPQ/DPQ correspond to ARM/Inter-SPQ/Intra-SPQ. The localized methodological revision is the reported training objective: v1's equally weighted cross-entropy terms become focal losses with class weights 1:4:6, gamma 2, and prediction/attention weights 1 and 0.5.

E1.justification: CS12K is renamed USC12K, retaining its 12,000 images, four scenes and source composition; the six generalization datasets also remain. v2 adds cross-task negative-detection scenarios on COD10K, NC4K, DUTS and HKU-IS, testing whether models incorrectly detect objects of the opposing attribute.

E2.justification: The 21-method quantitative benchmark and corresponding appendix comparator sets are retained. Figure 5 adds VSCode to the existing five qualitative comparators. UJSC receives new architectural discussion but is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds a protocol comparing five models using original pretrained weights versus USC12K-trained weights on opposite-task datasets, interpreting weighted F-measure against an expected value of zero and specifying VSCode's task prompts. The existing split, resolution, augmentation, training budget and generalization protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Tables 1 and 4 introduce a substantial diagnostic analysis: whether existing models confuse opposing attributes and whether USC12K training reduces that error. Existing component ablations, embedding visualizations and size analyses remain. The SAM-versus-SAM2 ablation moves from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 12 rather than being newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results. The new diagnostic tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds cross-task findings, including ICON's COD10K weighted F-measure of 0.6384 with original weights versus 0.0146 after USC12K training. In the retained benchmark, VSCode's reported mIoU changes from 69.78 to 74.17 and CSCS from 9.72 to 8.17; its saliency-metric row also changes. USCNet's headline scores, the six-dataset generalization results and ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the training objective changes from the cross-entropy sum in v1 Equation 4 to the weighted focal-loss objective in v2 Equations 4–5. CSCS's definition is unchanged. No new theorem, proof or formal guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The central dataset, model, metric and benchmark contributions remain. v2 adds explicit hypotheses about the causes of cross-task misdetection and a conclusion that USC12K training alleviates it. Renaming the dataset and prompt components does not itself establish additional contributions.

C2.justification: v2 develops new explanations involving conflicting attribute annotations, information loss and inadequate relationship modeling, and interprets the new experiments as evidence of reduced misdetection. It removes v1's detailed application discussion and explicit limitation concerning counting or separating individual instances, together with the proposed USCIS future direction.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the attention head's two 3-by-3 convolutions, query tensor shapes, linear downsampling and focal-loss hyperparameters. It also supplies a specific repository address where v1 only promises public release; both statements remain prospective. The detailed annotation workflow and principal hardware and training settings were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused positioning against UJSC's latent-space loss and VSCode's discrimination loss, emphasizing internal attribute interactions. UJSC was already cited in v1. The bibliography adds Lin et al.'s focal-loss paper and removes the masked-autoencoder reference; most other changes concern publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and conclusion around misdetection, revises method explanations and terminology, merges SAM subsections, and reorganizes experimental discussion. The appendix moves before the references, while the applications, difficulty and limitations sections are removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. v2 replaces Figure 1 with an architectural comparison, redraws the source chart, expands example and qualitative figures, splits the ablation table, and removes the instance-segmentation illustration. It adds two diagnostic tables and redisplays existing generalization results in a new summary table.

improvement.justification: The new cross-task experiments in Tables 1 and 4 strengthen the empirical motivation, while additional implementation details improve methodological clarity. These gains are limited by removal of the explicit instance-level limitation and the unexplained retention of identical USCNet scores despite the revised loss description. The principal benchmark evidence otherwise remains stable.
